headline: Progress Software ordered ShareFile customers to power down their servers against a credible active threat, while researchers showed a single PNG image can hijack AI coding agents and drain a repository's secrets.

emerging_trends.text: Attackers keep weaponizing AI coding agents, and the Ghostcommit technique shows a single booby-trapped PNG can slip past automated reviewers and drain a repository's secrets.

Web-facing enterprise software drew fire from every direction, from Progress ShareFile's emergency shutdown to a fresh Zimbra remote-code-execution bug and a global campaign against content management systems.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Progress Orders ShareFile Servers Shut Down

emerging_trends.text: Prosecutors closed in on ransomware crews as a Ryuk operator pleaded guilty in Oregon and a Blackcat/AlphV conspirator drew a federal prison sentence in Florida.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Ryuk and AlphV Members Face Justice

topics.title: Critical Zimbra Web Client Flaw
topics.latest_developments: Zimbra urged customers July 11, 2026 to patch a critical stored cross-site-scripting flaw in the Classic Web Client, still without a CVE, that lets a specially crafted email run malicious scripts and achieve arbitrary code execution inside a victim's session.
topics.summary: Zimbra runs email for governments and enterprises worldwide and draws frequent attacks; administrators should apply the update at once.

sources.title: Critical Zimbra Flaw Could Let Crafted Emails Run Malicious Code in User Sessions

topics.title: Australia Warns of Global CMS Campaign
topics.latest_developments: The Australian Cyber Security Centre issued an alert July 11, 2026 warning of a global campaign exploiting vulnerable content management systems and their plugins.
topics.summary: The ACSC flagged mass exploitation of outdated CMS platforms and add-ons that attackers use to plant web shells; site operators should patch core software and plugins and audit for compromise.

sources.title: Australia warns of global campaign targeting vulnerable CMS platforms

topics.title: Ghostcommit Poisons AI Code Reviewers
topics.latest_developments: Researchers unveiled Ghostcommit on July 11, 2026, a technique that buries a prompt injection inside a PNG image, sails past AI code reviewers CodeRabbit and Bugbot that never open image files, and tricks a coding agent into reading a repository's .env file and writing every secret into the code as a list of numbers.
topics.summary: The attack turns AI coding assistants into exfiltration tools; teams that let agents review or commit code should treat image files as untrusted input and cut off agent access to secrets.

sources.title: 'Ghostcommit' hides prompt injection in images to fool AI agents, steal secrets

topics.title: Progress Orders ShareFile Servers Shut Down
topics.latest_developments: Progress Software emailed ShareFile customers on July 10, 2026 to immediately power down the Windows servers running their Storage Zone Controllers over a 'credible external security threat,' and temporarily cut access to affected accounts out of an abundance of caution.
topics.summary: Storage Zone Controllers move files for the on-premises version of Progress's ShareFile secure file-sharing platform; administrators should shut the servers down and watch for guidance while Progress investigates.

sources.title: URGENT - Progress Tells ShareFile Customers to Shut Down Storage Zone Controllers Over Security Threat
Progress urges ShareFile admins to shut down servers over “credible” threat

topics.title: Ryuk and AlphV Members Face Justice
topics.latest_developments: A 34-year-old Armenian man pleaded guilty July 10, 2026 in Oregon federal court to conspiracy and computer fraud for deploying Ryuk ransomware against U.S. companies, facing up to 15 years, while a Florida court handed a Blackcat/AlphV conspirator a 70-month sentence for helping extort multiple victims.
topics.summary: Ryuk encrypted companies and hospitals across the U.S. at its peak, and AlphV ran one of the most prolific extortion operations; the two cases mark continued law-enforcement pressure on ransomware affiliates years after the crimes.

sources.title: Ryuk ransomware member pleads guilty in the US, faces 15 years in prison
Ryuk operator pleads guilty; Blackcat/AlphV conspirator gets nearly 6-year sentence

topics.title: New U-Boot Bootloader Flaws
topics.latest_developments: Researchers disclosed six vulnerabilities July 10, 2026 in the widely used U-Boot bootloader that let attackers run malicious code during device boot, opening the door to stealthy firmware attacks and persistent malware.
topics.summary: U-Boot boots countless embedded and IoT devices; the flaws let an attacker subvert security protections before the operating system loads, so device vendors need to ship firmware fixes.

sources.title: New U-Boot flaws could enable stealthy firmware attacks
